282:
(a) For purposes of ending the suffering of an abandoned domestic animal, which is hopelessly diseased or injured past recovery, a person may apply to the animal control officer for a decision regarding whether such animal should be destroyed.
(b) The order authorizing the destruction of such animal shall defeat an owner's claim for damages against the person destroying or procuring the destruction of such animal.
(Res. No. 2005-13, 7-5-05)
283:
Public livestock sales markets, livestock slaughter establishments, poultry dealers, poultry sales establishments, pet dealers, kennels, bird dealers, animal shelters and stables licensed by the state department of agriculture shall have an approved method and place for the disposal of dead animals and accessory waste material which die within the premises.
(Res. No. 2005-13, 7-5-05)
284:
Any person, firm, partnership or corporation, which violates any provision of this article, shall be guilty of a misdemeanor punishable as hereinafter set out in section 10-101 (penalties).
(Res. No. 2005-13, 7-5-05)
287:
No person shall intentionally abandon a dead dog on any private property belonging to another unless the person so doing shall have first obtained permission from the owner of the property on which the dog is being left and the provisions of section 10-31 are complied with in full.
(Res. No. 2005-13, 7-5-05)
288:
No person shall abandon a dead dog on any public property or public right-of-way unless the place in which the dog is being left is a public dump or other facility designed for receiving such and has been designated by county or municipal authorities as a public facility for receiving trash or refuse. The provisions of section 10-31 shall be complied with in full.
(Res. No. 2005-13, 7-5-05)
289:
No person shall release a dog on any property, public or private, with the intention of abandoning the dog.
(Res. No. 2005-13, 7-5-05)
290:
(a) The owner or, if no owner can be found, the custodian exercising care and control over any dog which goes upon the land of another and causes injury, death or damage directly or indirectly to livestock or poultry shall be civilly liable to the owner of the livestock or poultry for damages, death or injury caused by the dog. The liability of the owner or custodian of the dog shall include consequential damages.
(b) This section is to be considered cumulative of other remedies provided by law. There is no intent to do away with or limit other causes of action, which might inure to the owner of any livestock or poultry.
(Res. No. 2005-13, 7-5-05)
291:
(a) No person shall harm, maim, kill, attempt to kill or perform a cruel act on a dog except that a person may:
(1) Defend his person or property or the person or property of another from injury or damage being caused by a dog.
(2) Kill a dog causing injury or damage to livestock or poultry.
(b) The method used for killing a dog shall be designed to be as humane as is possible under the circumstances. A person who humanely kills a dog under the circumstances indicated in subsection (a) of this section shall incur no liability for such death.
(c) This section shall not be construed to limit the authority or duty of any law enforcement officer, animal control officer or veterinarian.
(Res. No. 2005-13, 7-5-05)
292:
The owner or custodian of a dog in heat shall provide an enclosure for the dog and shall not allow the dog to roam or run free.
(Res. No. 2005-13, 7-5-05)
293:
(a) As used in this section, the term:
(1) Animal shall not include any fish nor shall such term include any pest that might be exterminated or removed from a business, residence or other structure.
(2) Conviction shall include pleas of guilty, nolo contendere or probation as a first offender.
(3) Willful neglect means the intentional withholding of food, water, and necessary veterinarian care required by an animal to prevent starvation or dehydration.
(b) A person commits the offense of cruelty to animals by causing death or unjustifiable physical pain or suffering to an animal by an act, an omission or willful neglect. A person committing this offense may be cited pursuant to state law and be guilty of a misdemeanor if convicted, or may be cited for a county ordinance violation, and subject to the penalties as provided hereinafter. Any person convicted of a violation of this subsection shall be punished as hereinafter set out in section 10-101 (penalties) provided, however, that:
(1) A person who is convicted of a second violation of this section shall be punished as hereinafter set out in section 10-101 (penalties); and
(2) A person convicted of a third or subsequent violation of this section, or a violation which results in the death of an animal, shall be punished as hereinafter set out in section 10-101 (penalties).
(c) A person commits the offense of aggravated cruelty to animals when knowingly and maliciously causes death or physical harm to an animal by rendering a part of such animal's body useless or by seriously disfiguring such animal. A person convicted of the offense of aggravated cruelty to animals shall be punished as hereinafter set out in section 10-101 (penalties).
(d) Before sentencing a defendant for any conviction under this section, the sentencing judge may require psychological evaluation of the offender and shall consider the entire criminal record of the offender.
(e) The provisions of this section shall not be construed as prohibiting conduct which is otherwise permitted under the laws of the state or the United States, including, but not limited to, agricultural, animal husbandry, butchering, food processing, marketing, scientific research, medical, zoological, exhibition, competitive hunting, trapping, fishing, wildlife management, pest control practices or veterinary medicine. Nor to limit in any way the authority or duty of the department of agriculture, department of natural resources, any law enforcement officer, animal control officer, veterinarian or private landowner protecting one's property.
(f) Nothing in this section shall be construed as prohibiting a person from:
(1) Defending one's person or property, or the person or property of another, from injury or damage being caused by an animal.
(2) Injuring or killing an animal reasonably believed to constitute a threat for injury or damage to any person, property, livestock or poultry.
(g) The method used to injure or kill such animal shall be designed to be as humane as is possible under the circumstances. A person who humanely injures or kills an animal under the circumstances indicated in this subsection shall incur no civil or criminal liability for such injury or death.
(Res. No. 2005-13, 7-5-05; Res. No. 2007-33, 10-2-07)
294:
(a) A person commits the offense of dog fighting when he causes or allows a dog to fight another dog for sport or gaming purposes or maintains or operates any event at which dogs are allowed or encouraged to fight one another.
(b) A person convicted of the offense of dog fighting shall be punished as hereinafter set out in section 10-101 (penalties).
(Res. No. 2005-13, 7-5-05)
297:
(a) A dog that inflicts an injury upon a person when the dog is being used by a law enforcement officer to carry out the law enforcement officer's official duties shall not be declared a dangerous dog or potentially dangerous dog within the meaning of this article.
(b) A dog shall not be a dangerous dog or a potentially dangerous dog if the injury inflicted by the dog was sustained by a person who was:
(1) An adult committing a willful trespass or other tort.
(2) Tormenting, abusing or assaulting the dog or had in the past been observed or reported to have tormented, abused or assaulted the dog.
(3) Committing or attempting to commit a crime.
(Res. No. 2005-13, 7-5-05)
298:
(a) The county's jurisdiction for the enforcement of this article shall be the unincorporated area of the county and within the corporate limits of the City of Cleveland or the City of Helen subject to an agreement with each municipality for animal control services and for the joint use of personnel, facilities and equipment used in the provision of such services.
(b) The person carrying out the duties of an animal control officer shall not be authorized to make arrests unless the person is a law enforcement officer having the powers of arrest.
(c) The board of commissioners may provide by resolution for the creation of an animal control board to hold hearings provided for in section 10-54. If such an animal control board is created, such board may hear and determine matters provided for in section 10-54. An animal control board may be created by two or more of the local governments.
(Res. No. 2005-13, 7-5-05)
299:
(a) Upon receiving a report of a dangerous dog or potentially dangerous dog, the animal control officer shall make such investigations and inquiries as necessary to carry out the provisions of this article.
(b) When an animal control officer classifies a dog as a dangerous dog or reclassifies a potentially dangerous dog as a dangerous dog, the animal control officer shall contact the dog's owner in writing by personal service of the notice by the animal control officer or by the county sheriff's department, or by certified mail, return receipt requested, to the owner's last known address, of such classification or reclassification. If the owner cannot be located, or if the certified letter is refused or the return receipt is returned unsigned for any reason, or if the owner is avoiding service of the notice, then the animal control officer may give notice of the classification or reclassification to the dog's owner by way of publication.
(Res. No. 2005-13, 7-5-05; Res. No. 2007-33, 10-2-07)
300:
(a) As applied to the owners of potentially dangerous dogs, the procedures provided for in this section must be carried out as a necessary condition for the enforcement of the provisions of this article. As applied to the owners of dangerous dogs, the procedures provided for in this section shall not be an essential element of any crime provided for in this article.
(b) When a dangerous dog or a potentially dangerous dog is classified as such, the animal control officer shall notify the dog's owner of such classification. If the owner of the dog is not identified within 72 hours, the dog shall be euthanized.
(c) The notice to the owner shall meet the following requirements:
(1) The notice shall be in writing and mailed by certified mail to the owner's last known address.
(2) The notice shall include a summary of the animal control officer's findings that formed the basis for the dog's classification as a dangerous or potentially dangerous dog.
(3) The notice shall be dated and shall state that the owner, within 15 days after the date shown on the notice, has a right to request in writing a hearing on the animal control officer's determination that the dog is a dangerous dog or potentially dangerous dog.
(4) The notice shall state that the hearing, if requested, shall be before the governing authority of the local government having jurisdiction or the animal control board, if created.
(5) The notice shall state that if a hearing is not requested, the animal control officer's determination that the dog is a dangerous dog or a potentially dangerous dog will become effective on the date specified in the notice, which shall be after the last day on which the owner has a right to request a hearing.
(d) When the appropriate governing body or animal control board receives a request for a hearing as provided in subsection (c) of this section, it shall schedule such hearing within 30 days after receiving the request. The governing body or board shall notify the dog owner in writing by certified mail of the date, time, and place of the hearing, and such notice shall be mailed to the dog owner at least 10 days prior to the date of the hearing.
(e) At the hearing, the owner of the dog shall be given the opportunity to testify and present evidence. In addition, the governing authority or board shall receive such other evidence and hear such other testimony as the governing body or animal control board may find reasonably necessary to make a determination to sustain, modify or overrule the animal control officer's classification of the dog.
(f) Within ten days after the date of the hearing, the governing body or animal control board shall notify the dog owner in writing by certified mail of its determination on the matter. If such determination is that the dog is a dangerous dog or a potentially dangerous dog, the notice shall specify the date upon which that determination is effective.
(Res. No. 2005-13, 7-5-05)
301:
(a) It is unlawful for an owner to have or possess within the county a dangerous dog or potentially dangerous dog without a certificate of registration issued in accordance with the provisions of this section.
(b) Subject to the additional requirements of subsection (c) of this section for dangerous dogs, the animal control officer shall issue a certificate of registration to the owner of such dog if the owner notifies the animal control officer or the animal control officer otherwise finds sufficient evidence of:
(1) A proper enclosure to confine the dangerous dog or potentially dangerous dog; and
(2) The posting of the premises where the dangerous dog or potentially dangerous dog is located with a clearly visible sign warning that there is a dangerous dog on the property. The sign required shall conform substantially to the design provided by the department of natural resources.
(c) In addition to the requirements of subsection (b) of this section, the owner of a dangerous dog shall present to the animal control officer evidence of:
(1) A policy for insurance in the amount of at least $500,000.00 with a maximum deductible of $100.00 issued by an insurer authorized and approved by the state insurance commissioner to transact business in the state that insures the owner of the dangerous dog against liability for any personal injuries including but not limited to death, and property damage inflicted by the dangerous dog. A dangerous dog has the potential of deadly force, and for this reason liability insurance policies that unduly restrict coverage as to any personal injuries and property damage as determined by the animal control officer shall be deemed to not meet the insurance requirements of this subsection. The determination of the animal control officer as to whether the exclusion unduly restricts the liability coverage will be based upon the following facts:
a. A dangerous dog is capable of deadly force;
b. The intent of this subsection is that there be liability coverage for any personal injuries including death and any property damage inflicted by the dangerous dog;
c. The nature of the exclusions contained within the policy; and
d. Any other reasonable factor that may be considered in achieving the intent of this subsection that there be liability insurance coverage for any personal injuries including death and any property damage inflicted by the dangerous dog; or
(2) A surety bond in the amount of at least $500,000.00 issued by a surety company authorized to transact business in the State of Georgia, and with the bond issued to the dog's owner providing that it is payable to any person or persons that have suffered any personal injuries including but not limited to death and property damage inflicted by the dangerous dog. A dangerous dog has the potential of deadly force, and for this reason surety bonds that unduly restrict coverage as to any personal injuries and property damage as determined by the animal control officer shall be deemed to not meet the liability bond requirements of this subsection. The determination of the animal control officer as to whether the exclusion unduly restricts the liability bond coverage will be based upon the following facts:
a. A dangerous dog is capable of deadly force;
b. The intent of this subsection is that there be liability bond coverage for any personal injuries and any property damage inflicted by the dangerous dog;
c. The nature of the exclusions contained within the bond; and
d. Any other reasonable factor that may be considered in achieving the intent of this subsection that there be liability bond coverage for any personal injuries and any property damage inflicted by the dangerous dog; and
(3) A copy of the policy (and not the insurance binder) or surety bond for approval. Insurance coverage provided by a surplus line insurance carrier, shall be accompanied by a certification by the office of the state insurance commissioner that the specific surplus line insurance carrier, including but not limited to any specific group or subgroup of Lloyd's of London, is on the approved list for surplus line insurance carriers maintained by the state insurance commissioner pursuant to O.C.G.A. § 33-5-25.
(d) The owner of a dangerous dog or potentially dangerous dog shall notify the animal control officer within 24 hours if the dog is loose, unconfined, attacked a human, died or has been sold or donated. If the dog has been sold or donated, the owner shall also provide the animal control officer with the name, address and telephone number of the new owner of the dog.
(e) The owner of a dangerous dog or potentially dangerous dog shall notify the animal control officer if the owner is moving from the animal control officer's jurisdiction. The owner of a dangerous dog or potentially dangerous dog who is a new resident of the county shall register the dog as required in this section within ten days after becoming a resident.
(f) The issuance or renewal of a certificate of registration does not warrant or guarantee that the requirements specified in subsections (b) and (c) of this section are maintained on a continuous basis following the date of the issuance of the initial certificate of registration or following the date of any annual renewal of such certificate.
(g) An animal control officer is authorized to make whatever inquiry is deemed necessary to ensure compliance with the provisions of this article.
(h) Certificates of registration shall be renewed on an annual basis. At the time of the annual renewal of a certificate of registration, the animal control officer shall require evidence that the dangerous dog or potentially dangerous dog is continuing to be confined in a proper enclosure and that the owner is continuing to comply with other provisions of this article.
(Res. No. 2005-13, 7-5-05; Res. No. 2007-33, 10-2-07)
302:
(a) It is unlawful for an owner of a dangerous dog to permit the dog to be outside a proper enclosure unless the dog is muzzled and restrained by a substantial chain or leash and is under the physical restraint of a responsible person. The muzzle shall be made in a manner that will not cause injury to the dog or interfere with its vision or respiration but will prevent it from biting a person.
(b) It is unlawful for the owner of a potentially dangerous dog to permit the dog to be outside a proper enclosure unless the dog is restrained by a substantial chain or leash and is under the restraint of a responsible person.
(Res. No. 2005-13, 7-5-05)
303:
(a) A dangerous dog shall be immediately confiscated by the animal control officer if the:
(1) Owner of the dog does not secure the liability insurance or bond required by subsection (c) of section 10-55.
(2) Dog is not validly registered as required by section 10-55.
(3) Dog is not maintained in a proper enclosure.
(4) Dog is outside a proper enclosure in violation of subsection (a) of section 10-56.
(b) A potentially dangerous dog shall be confiscated in the same manner as a dangerous dog if the dog is:
(1) Not validly registered as required by section 10-55.
(2) Not maintained in a proper enclosure.
(3) Outside of a proper enclosure in violation of subsection (b) of section 10-56.
(c) Any dog that has been confiscated under the provisions of subsection (a) or (b) of this section shall be returned to its owner upon the owner's compliance with the provisions of this article and upon the payment of reasonable confiscation costs. In the event the owner has not complied with the provisions of this article within ten days of the date the dog was confiscated, said dog shall be destroyed in an expeditious and humane manner.
(Res. No. 2005-13, 7-5-05)
304:
(a) The owner of a dangerous dog who violates the applicable provisions of section 10-55 or section 10-56 or whose dangerous dog is subject to confiscation under subsection (a) of section 10-57 shall be punished as hereinafter set out in section 10-101 (penalties) or in the alternative may be cited pursuant to state law and if convicted shall be subject to the penalties for misdemeanors of a high and aggravated nature. In addition to any confinement that might be imposed for a conviction under this subsection, a second conviction shall require the mandatory penalties as hereinafter set out in section 10-101 (Penalties), and a third or subsequent conviction shall require the mandatory penalties hereinafter set out in section 10-101 (penalties).
(b) The owner of a potentially dangerous dog who violates the applicable provisions of section 10-55 or section 10-56 or whose potentially dangerous dog is subject to confiscation under subsection (b) of section 10-57 shall be punished as hereinafter set out in section 10-101 (penalties) or in the alternative may be cited to state law and if convicted shall be subject to the penalties for a misdemeanor. In addition to any confinement that might be imposed for a conviction under this subsection, a second conviction shall require the mandatory penalties as hereinafter set out in section 10-101 (Penalties), and for a third or subsequent conviction shall require the mandatory penalties as hereinafter set out in section 10-101 (penalties).
(c) If an owner who has a previous conviction for a violation of this chapter knowingly and willfully fails to comply with the provisions of this chapter, such owner shall be guilty of a felony under state law, and may be cited pursuant to state law if the owner's dangerous dog attacks or bits a human being under circumstances constituting another violation of this chapter. In the discretion of the animal control officer or any duly certified law enforcement officer, in the alternative, the owner of the dangerous dog may be cited for an ordinance violation and may be punished as hereinafter set out in section 10-101 (penalties).
(d) An owner who knowingly and willfully fails to comply with the provisions of this chapter shall be guilty of a felony under state law, and in the discretion of the animal control officer or any duly certified law enforcement officer, may be cited pursuant to state law if the owner's dangerous dog aggressively attacks and causes severe injury or death of a human being under circumstances constituting a violation of this chapter. In the alternative, and in the discretion of the animal control officer, the animal control officer may cite the owner of a dangerous dog for a violation of this ordinance subsection, and the owner of the dangerous dog shall be punished as hereinafter set out in section 10-101 (penalties).
(e) In addition to the penalties for violations under subsection (c) or (d) of this section, the dangerous dog involved shall be immediately confiscated by the animal control officer and placed in quarantine. Thereafter, the dangerous dog shall be destroyed in an expeditious and humane manner.
(Res. No. 2005-13, 7-5-05; Res. No. 2007-33, 10-2-07)
305:
(a) It is the intent that the owner of a dangerous dog or potentially dangerous dog shall be solely liable for any injury to or death of a person caused by such dog.
(b) Under no circumstances shall the county, the animal control officer or an employee or official of the county which enforces or fails to enforce the provisions of this article be held liable for any damages:
(1) To any person who suffers an injury inflicted by a dog that has been identified as being a dangerous dog or potentially dangerous dog.
(2) By a dog that has been reported to the proper authorities as being a dangerous dog or potentially dangerous dog.
(3) By a dog that a local government has failed to identify as a dangerous dog or potentially dangerous dog.
(4) By a dog which has been identified as being a dangerous dog or potentially dangerous dog but has not been kept or restrained in the manner described in section 10-55(b).
(5) By a dangerous dog or potentially dangerous dog, whose owner has not maintained insurance coverage or a surety bond as required in section 10-55(c).
(Res. No. 2005-13, 7-5-05)
308:
(a) It shall be unlawful for any person to act as a pet dealer or operate a kennel, stable or animal shelter unless such person has a valid license issued by the commissioner of agriculture. Any person acting without a license in violation of this section shall be guilty of a misdemeanor.
(b) Any person licensed by the commissioner of agriculture as a bird dealer shall not be required to obtain a license under this article if such person does not deal in animals other than birds. If, however, a licensed bird dealer sells, offers to sell, exchanges or offers for adoption dogs, cats, fish, reptiles or other animals customarily obtained as pets, then such dealer shall be required to obtain a license under this article in addition to his bird dealer's license.
(c) A license must be prominently displayed at each place of business of a pet dealer and at each kennel, stable and animal shelter.
(Res. No. 2005-13, 7-5-05)
309:
(a) In the control, suppression, prevention and eradication of animal diseases, the animal control officer shall be authorized to quarantine an animal, premises or any area when it is determined:
(1) The animals are infected with a contagious or infectious disease.
(2) The place is in an unsanitary condition, which might cause the spread of disease.
(3) An animal has or has been exposed to any contagious or infectious disease.
(b) The animal control officer is authorized to issue and enforce stop sale, stop use or stop movement orders to the owners or custodians of any animals, ordering them to hold animals at a designated place, when the animal control officer finds such animals to:
(1) Be infected with or to have been exposed to any contagious or infectious disease.
(2) Be held by a person whose license has expired.
(3) Be held by a person who has failed to obtain a license within ten days of the date on which written notice of the need to obtain a license was given by the animal control officer.
(c) It shall be unlawful for any person to sell, use or move any animal in violation of any quarantine or stop sale, stop use or stop removal order issued under this section.
(Res. No. 2005-13, 7-5-05)
310:
(a) The animal control officer is authorized to enter upon any public or private property for the purpose of inspecting the business premises of any pet dealer, animal shelter, kennel or stable to determine if such facility is licensed and for the purpose of enforcing this article.
(b) At any time, there is probable cause to believe that a violation of this article or any rule or regulation adopted pursuant to this article has occurred; a law enforcement officer may apply to the appropriate court for an inspection warrant.
(c) The animal control officer is authorized to impound any animal:
(1) That has not received humane care.
(2) That has been subjected to cruelty in violation of section 10-47 (cruelty to animals)
(3) That is used or intended for use in any violation of section 10-48 (dog fighting).
(4) If it is determined that consent order or other order concerning the treatment of animals issued pursuant to this article is being violated.
(Res. No. 2005-13, 7-5-05)
311:
(a) It shall be the duty of any person impounding an animal under this article to immediately serve the owner, if known, of such animal with a notice of impoundment. Such notice shall contain:
(1) The name and business address of the person impounding the animal.
(2) The name and address of the agency retaining custody of the animal.
(3) A description of the animal.
(4) The reason the animal was impounded.
(5) A statement regarding the time limitations for the owner to request a hearing as provided in for section 10-65.
(b) The notice shall be provided by certified mail sent to the last known address of the owner.
(c) Whenever under this chapter service is required or permitted to be made upon a party represented by an attorney, the service shall be made upon the attorney unless the court orders service upon the party.
(d) If the owner of such animal is unknown or cannot be found, service of the notice of impoundment shall be made by posting the notice in a conspicuous place at the location where the animal was found and impounded and by publishing a notice once in a newspaper of general circulation.
(e) An animal impounded pursuant to this article is deemed to be in the custody of the county.
(Res. No. 2005-13, 7-5-05)
312:
(a) If the owner of an impounded animal fails to respond in writing within five business days of the date the notice of impoundment was served or if the owner is unknown or could not be found within 30 days of publication of the notice of impoundment, the impounded animal shall be disposed of pursuant to section 10-30.
(b) If the owner of an impounded animal refuses to enter into a consent agreement ensuring that the animal will be given humane care and adequate and veterinary care, the owner may request, in writing, a hearing within five business days of the date the notice of impoundment was served.
(c) If no hearing is requested within the time limits specified and the failure to request such hearing is due in whole or in part to a reasonably avoidable fault of the owner, the right to a hearing shall have been waived.
(d) Within 30 days after receiving a written request for a hearing, the applicable governing body or animal control board shall conduct a hearing. The hearing shall be public and all testimony shall be received under oath.
(e) The scope of the hearing shall be limited to whether the impounding of the animal was authorized by section 10-63.
(f) The governing body or animal control board shall within five business days after such hearing forward a decision to the owner and the animal control officer.
(g) If the governing body or animal control board finds that the animal was improperly impounded, the animal shall be returned to the owner and the cost incurred shall be paid by the county.
(h) If the governing body or animal control board finds that the animal was lawfully impounded, the governing body or animal control board shall rule that:
(1) The animal be disposed of as provided herein.
(2) The animal be returned to the owner.
(3) If the owner has previously been found guilty of failure to provide humane care to an animal, committed cruelty to animals or engaged in dog fighting, the return may be conditioned on the following:
a. Such animal will be given humane care and adequate veterinary services.
b. Such animal not be subjected to mistreatment.
c. The owner complying with this article.
(i) The provisions of this section shall not apply to an animal that was an object or instrumentality of a crime nor shall any such animal be returned to the owner or disposed of without the approval of the prosecuting attorney.
(Res. No. 2005-13, 7-5-05)
313:
The provisions of this article shall not apply to any person who raises, keeps or maintains animals solely for the purposes of human consumption.
(Res. No. 2005-13, 7-5-05)
314:
In addition to the remedies provided in this article or elsewhere in the laws of the state or the county and notwithstanding the existence of an adequate remedy at law, the county attorney is authorized to apply to the superior court for an injunction or restraining order. The court shall for good cause shown grant a temporary or permanent injunction or an ex parte or restraining order, restraining or enjoining any person, partnership, firm, corporation, or other entity from violating and continuing to violate this article. Such injunction or restraining order shall be issued without bond and may be granted notwithstanding the fact that the violation constitutes a criminal act and notwithstanding the pendency of any criminal prosecution for the same violation.
(Res. No. 2005-13, 7-5-05)
315:
(a) A licensed veterinarian having reasonable cause to believe that an animal has been subjected to animal cruelty or dog fighting may make or cause to be made a report of such violation to the animal control officer.
(b) Any person participating in the making of a report pursuant to this section or participating in any administrative or judicial proceeding pursuant to this article shall be immune from any civil or criminal liability that might otherwise be imposed, provided such participation is made in good faith.
(Res. No. 2005-13, 7-5-05)
316:
The animal control officer shall be required to provide timely written notice to the commissioner of agriculture for enforcement action taken against an operator who is licensed by and who is alleged to be in violation of department of agriculture rules and regulations. The department shall be notified of the initiation of any such local enforcement action and of the conclusions or ultimate outcome of any such action.
(Res. No. 2005-13, 7-5-05)
317:
A person violating the provisions of this chapter shall be punished as hereinafter set out in section 10-101 (penalties). In the alternative, and in the discretion of the animal control officer, the person may be cited with a violation of state law, and be guilty of a misdemeanor if convicted.
(1) Each violation of this article shall constitute a separate offense.
(Res. No. 2005-13, 7-5-05; Res. No. 2007-33, 10-2-07)
